abilities.name: Wrath of Pallas
abilities.description: Lashes out at a structure. Costs divinity equal to the power; at power 2 it damages a target without setting it alight.

abilities.name: Counsel
abilities.description: Gives counsel or a judgment, told aloud to everyone present and recorded as a legend.

abilities.name: Gift of the Olive
abilities.description: Answers a mortal's prayer for help with what it needs.

relationships.note: They contested Attica and the twelve gods gave it to her. The starting value is authored tuning.
Hera sends her to check Achilles, and they once wished with Poseidon to bind Zeus. The starting value is authored tuning.
He brought her forth from his head and bars the gods from the war; she obeys and still advises. The starting value is authored tuning.

lore.statement: Zeus brings Athena forth himself, from his own head: bright-eyed Tritogeneia.
She is hailed as Pallas Athena, bright-eyed, inventive, unbending of heart, a pure virgin and saviour of cities.
Sent from heaven by Hera, Athena takes Achilles by his fair hair and checks him from drawing his sword on Agamemnon, bidding him use words instead.
Poseidon and Athena contested Attica: he struck the acropolis and brought up a sea, she planted an olive with Cecrops as witness, and the twelve gods awarded the land to her.
At Athens she is shown with the olive plant and Poseidon with the wave, and the contest fills the rear pediment of her temple.
Hera, Poseidon, and Pallas Athena once wished to put Zeus in bonds.
Zeus forbids the gods to join the fighting at Troy. Athena says they will keep out of the fight, though they may advise the Argives.
Athena wears a soft embroidered robe that she herself wrought, and she and Hephaestus teach crafts to men.

variants.note: Apollodorus gives Poseidon a sea at the acropolis and Athena an olive; Pausanias shows the olive and the wave. Both give Athena the olive, and the profile keeps only that.
Apollodorus has the twelve gods judge the contest and rejects the tellings that name Cecrops and Cranaus, or Erysichthon, as the judges. The profile keeps the twelve gods.

inventions.statement: Athena's domain troubles are the game's own.
inventions.reason: A loom that breaks and a tool flaw that ruins craftwork are troubles the game draws on a season's odds and a floor, damaging the loom house or taking goods. The sources attest her craft (weaving, the craftsman's skill); no source tells these episodes.

inventions.statement: Athena's counsel is told in play as a legend.
inventions.reason: Legend is the world's only action that records speech; it is a game mapping, not a mythic device.

inventions.statement: Her wrath is a damaging strike on structures, below the ignition threshold.
inventions.reason: The world has no action that harms a person. This mapping is a game stand-in.

inventions.statement: Her gift to a mortal who prays is the world's bless action.
inventions.reason: The world's one way to help a mortal is to bless it; the sources give her gift as the olive, which the game does not model.

inventions.statement: The olive growers and weavers who revere her, and the grove they work by the ancient olive tree, are placed by the game.
inventions.reason: The sources link her to the olive and to weaving but give no town of growers. The livelihoods are an invention.

inventions.statement: The drive weights and the starting dispositions of Athena are authored tuning.
inventions.reason: The sources describe temperament in prose; the numbers are a design choice to be revised against play.

troubles.statement: A loom breaks: the loom house is damaged. Winter.
A flaw in a tool ruins craftwork: tools or planks are lost. Spring and autumn.
